3.text: The number of days which must elapse between the first and the last per-

4.text: formance is the same as in the birth ceremonial. After five days, the people

5.text: visit the corpse again to see if wild beasts have at last mutilated the body.

6.text: On the return from this visit, the whole camp arranges the feast of antlers,

7.text: even though it may be quite out of season. If antlers are scarce, they

8.text: gather together all the loose ones that can be found, though the use of such

9.text: antlers for the antler ceremonial is generally forbidden.

10.text: On coming back from the second visit, the family move their tent to

14.text: Still later the chief of the funeral procession must perform additional

15.text: incantations in order to protect himself from being pursued by the deceased.

16.text: To give an illustration of this, he will some time during the following

17.text: summer wade through the water in a pool, proclaiming aloud, “I am not a

18.text: man: I am a white gull, I am an eider-duck.” If he should fail to do this,

19.text: a dangerous illness would be sure to attack him.

20.text: Such is a typical performance of the funeral ceremony of a Reindeer

21.text: Chukchee, with exposure of the corpse in the open country, and with much

22.text: slaughtering for sacrifice. For the poorer people, of course, all the details

23.text: are much simplified. The bodies of the deceased who “go away afoot” will

24.text: not be covered with meat. After the cutting of the clothes, two pieces will

25.text: be left on the body, — one covering the face, and the other covering the

26.text: genitalia. The bodies of small children are sometimes cut to pieces and

27.text: scattered in all directions. The purpose of this is to show to the World
